**Natural-language hypothesis (final):** Across ML-enabled system projects, **Interviews** is the most commonly used technique for eliciting requirements. In this dataset it is reported by 50.53 % of the 188 survey respondents who completed the questionnaire (95 % bootstrap percentile CI: [43.60 %, 57.45 %], B = 10,000, seed-fixed), leading the next-most-used technique — Prototyping at 39.89 % — by 10.64 percentage points. The result is robust to the choice of denominator: 51.83 % (CI [43.90 %, 59.76 %]) on the strict subset of n = 164 fully-completed respondents and 50.00 % (CI [42.78 %, 57.22 %]) when filtering only on the `-77` sentinel (n = 194), with a plurality gap over the runner-up of 12.81 pp and 11.34 pp respectively.

**Note on the question's headline figure (openly disclosed as agreed):** The supplied 69.399 % (95 % CI [69.062, 69.735]) cannot be reproduced on this dataset under any of the standard respondent aggregations — none of n = 164 / 188 / 200 / 246 / 276 produces a clean integer count at 69.4 %, and the stated CI width of 0.67 pp is roughly an order of magnitude narrower than a binomial asymptotic width for n ≈ 188 (≈ 14 pp). The 69.4 % figure most plausibly reflects the source study's specific analytical choices (different denominator such as respondents with role × completed duration > 0, weighting, item-framing, or pre-registration pool). We report both the published headline value and the data-supported figure rather than asserting agreement.

**Operationalization (for reproducibility):** "Most commonly used" is defined as the technique with the largest share of respondents whose Q9 indicator equals `quoted`, restricted to non-suspended respondents (`Status ∈ {"Completed (31)", "Completed after break (32)"}`; n = 188). The catch-all `Q9_ML_Elicitation_Others` is excluded from the ranking. `Q9_ML_Elicitation_Others_Free` is a free-text column treated as qualitative note only.
